'''Rustem F. Ismagilov''' is a Russian-American chemist. He is the Ethel Wilson Bowles and Robert Bowles Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering at the [[California Institute of Technology]].

==Early life and education==
Ismagilov was born in 1973 in Ufa, Russia. He received his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in chemistry in 1994 from the [[Higher Chemical College of the Russian Academy of Sciences]] before moving to the United States. In 1998, he received a Ph.D. in chemistry from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] while working with Stephen F. Nelson.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Fabrication inside Microchannels Using Fluid Flow |journal=[[Accounts of Chemical Research]] |date=April 18, 2000 |volume=33 |pages=841–847 |doi=10.1021/ar000062u |pmid=11123883 |url=https://gmwgroup.harvard.edu/files/gmwgroup/files/697.pdf |access-date=October 10, 2021|last1=Kenis |first1=P. J. |last2=Ismagilov |first2=R. F. |last3=Takayama |first3=S. |last4=Whitesides |first4=G. M. |last5=Li |first5=S. |last6=White |first6=H. S. |issue=12 }}</ref> Following his Ph.D., Ismagilov was a Postdoctoral Fellow with the Whitesides Research Group at [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Whitesides Research Group |url=https://gmwgroup.harvard.edu/resources |publisher=Harvard University |access-date=October 10, 2021}}</ref>

==Career==
Ismagilov joined the faculty at the [[University of Chicago]] in 2001 as an [[assistant professor]].<ref name="ACS">{{cite web |last1=Henry Arnaud |first1=Celia |title=ACS Award in Pure Chemistry |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/86/i4/ACS-Award-Pure-Chemistry.html |publisher=[[Chemical & Engineering News]] |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=January 28, 2008}}</ref> While working in this role, he focused his research on the chemical complexity of biological systems using microfabrication and microfluidics as synthetic tools.<ref name="Dreyfus">{{cite web |last1=Koppes |first1=Steve |title=Chemistry professor receives Dreyfus |url=http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/011101/dreyfus.shtml |publisher=Chicago Chronicle |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=November 1, 2001}}</ref> As a result, he received a five-year, $40,000 award from [[The Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation]]<ref name="Dreyfus"/> and became a 2002 [[Searle Scholars Program|Searle Scholar]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Koppes |first1=Steve |title=Ismagilov named 2002 Searle Scholar |url=http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/020815/searle.shtml |publisher=Chicago Chronicle |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=August 15, 2002}}</ref> The following year, Ismagilov received a three-year grant from the [[Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation]] to study "the use of microfluidics to control chemical systems in a time-dependent fashion."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Koppes |first1=Steve |title=Chemistry professor receives three-year Beckman grant |url=http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/030515/beckman.shtml |publisher=Chicago Chronicle |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=May 15, 2003}}</ref> While conducting his research, he was a recipient of the 2003 [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]],<ref>{{cite web |title=White House Announces 2003 Awards for Early Career Scientists and Engineers |url=https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/news/releases/2004/09/text/20040909-9.html |publisher=White House |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=September 9, 2004}}</ref> 2005 [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award]],<ref>{{cite web |title=PROFESSOR ISMAGILOV WAS NAMED A RECIPIENT OF THE 2005 ARTHUR C. COPE SCHOLAR AWARD FROM THE AMERICAN CHEMICAL SOCIETY. |date=9 January 2012 |url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/news/professor-ismagilov-was-named-a-recipient-of-the-2005-arthur-c-cope-scholar-award-from-the |publisher=University of Chicago |access-date=October 10, 2021}}</ref> and was listed among the world’s 100 Top Young Innovators for 2004.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Koppes |first1=Steve |title=Chemist garners three awards, including White House honor |url=http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/040923/ismagilov.shtml |publisher=Chicago Chronicle |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=September 23, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kopppes |first1=Steve |title=Technology Review magazine names Rustem Ismagilov one of world's top young innovators, his third recognition in one month |url=http://www-news.uchicago.edu/releases/04/040920.ismagilov.shtml |publisher=Chicago Chronicle |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=September 20, 2004}}</ref>

Ismagilov was promoted to the rank of [[associate professor]] of chemistry in 2005.<ref name="ACS"/> Following his promotion, he co-developed a microfluidics technique to find medical-diagnostic applications.<ref>{{cite web |title=University of Chicago team successfully uses chemistry to predict the dynamics of clotting in human blood: Microfluidics technique could find medical-diagnostic applications |url=http://www-news.uchicago.edu/releases/06/061016.clotting.shtml |publisher=Chicago Chronicle |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=October 16, 2006}}</ref> He also developed a microfluidic device called SlipChip as a method for precise quantification of nucleic acids in resource-limited settings.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Madeleine |title=Using $15M DARPA Award, Caltech Team Shows Robust Digital Isothermal PCR on 'SlipChip' Device |url=https://www.genomeweb.com/pcrsample-prep/using-15m-darpa-award-caltech-team-shows-robust-digital-isothermal-pcr-slipchip |publisher=Genome Web |access-date=October 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141009094152/https://www.genomeweb.com/pcrsample-prep/using-15m-darpa-award-caltech-team-shows-robust-digital-isothermal-pcr-slipchip |archive-date=October 9, 2014 |date=December 5, 2013}}</ref> In 2008, Ismagilov was the recipient of the [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Pure Chemistry, which recognizes significant research done by young scientists.<ref name="ACS"/> By 2011, Ismagilov was listed by Clarivate as being amongst the most influential 100 chemists based on the highest citation impact scores for chemistry papers published from 2000 to 2010.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Koppes |first1=Steve |title=Faculty members garner honors, recognition during International Year of Chemistry |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/faculty-members-garner-honors-recognition-during-international-year-chemistry |publisher=University of Chicago |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=April 18, 2011}}</ref> He was also elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web |title=American Association for the Advancement of Science elects four UChicago fellows |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/american-association-advancement-science-elects-four-uchicago-fellows |publisher=University of Chicago |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=April 26, 2011}}</ref>

=== California Institute of Technology ===
Ismagilov left the [[University of Chicago]] in 2012 to become the John W. and Herberta M. Miles Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering. He was a 2012 winner of the Wisconsin Alumni Association’s Forward under 40 award<ref>{{cite web |title=Rustem Ismagilov PhD'98 |url=https://www.uwalumni.com/news/forward_ismagilov/ |publisher=Wisconsin Alumni Association |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=March 1, 2012}}</ref> and received Caltech's Richard P. Feynman Excellence in Teaching Award in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/ismagilov-receives-feynman-prize|title=Rustem Ismagilov Receives Feynman Prize for Excellence in Teaching|website=California Institute of Technology|date=2024-02-29|access-date=2026-10-22}}</ref>

In 2013, Ismagilov was appointed the Director of the Jacobs Institute for Molecular Engineering for Medicine.<ref>{{Cite web |title=People - Jacobs Institute |url=https://jacobsinstitute.caltech.edu/people |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=jacobsinstitute.caltech.edu}}</ref> 

In 2021, Ismagilov was appointed a Professor for the Merkin Institute for Translational Research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=People |url=http://merkin.caltech.edu/people |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=Merkin Institute for Translational Research |language=en}}</ref> 

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Ismagilov's laboratory launched a large, community-based study of COVID-19 transmission<ref>{{cite web |last1=Velasco |first1=Emily |title=Researchers Partner with Pasadena Public Health on COVID-19 Study |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/researchers-partner-with-pasadena-public-health-on-covid-19-study |publisher=The Caltech Weekly |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}}</ref>, enrolling more than 400 participants between 2020-2022<ref>https://covid-study.caltech.edu/</ref>. Early results from the study were profiled in The New York Times.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/22/science/omicron-covid-testing.html|title=Combined nasal and throat testing swabs would detect more Omicron infections, two papers suggest.|first=Emily|last=Anthes|work=The New York Times|date=2022-07-22|access-date=2026-10-22}}</ref>
